svg.aria-label: Who owns what: a matrix of six cross-cutting rules against four columns. Three columns are the exit proofs and all three are unfiled placeholders — the Devtool checklist, the DevForce proof path and the multi-seat collab scenario. The fourth column is FIX-1467, the exploration that is Done and merged. Row ER-1, a non-human seat owns the task: the collab column owns it, the Devtool column consumes it, the DevForce column consumes it, FIX-1467 is blank. Row ER-2, Waiting-on-you is parked with a reason: the Devtool column owns it and is marked checklist row 4, the collab column consumes it, FIX-1467 and DevForce are blank. Row ER-3, every proof runs on a live hired Workforce: the DevForce column owns it because its path stands the workforce up, and the Devtool and collab columns consume it. Row ER-4, every proof composes and adds no layer: all three proof columns are marked builds if filed. Row ER-18, the downstream-blocking walls: FIX-1467's cell is marked MET, with the noun, the migration and the grant model all answered by its merge, and the Devtool column consumes it at checklist row 6. Last row, the done condition, now three separate rules: the Devtool column holds ER-Devtool marked NO CHILD, the DevForce column holds ER-DevForce marked NO CHILD, and the collab column holds ER-Collab marked NO CHILD — three empty cells on the diagonal, and the done condition owned in zero parts. A legend distinguishes the one committed owner, a consumes cell that must not be re-decided, a conditional cell that applies once the row is filed, a MET cell, and a NO CHILD cell where nothing in the set produces the rule; a blank cell means the row does not touch that rule. Notes record that kitchen-sink FIX-1455 no longer has a column because it left the set on September 20, that ER-1, ER-2 and ER-3 were re-owned rather than left pointing at it, that ER-15 was rewritten and ER-19 retired, and that nineteen further rules bind every row equally and need no column.
svg.text: WHO OWNS WHAT — ALL THREE EXIT PROOFS HAVE NO CHILD

g.text: ER-1 · a non-human seat owns the task
ER-2 · Waiting-on-you is parked, with a reason
ER-3 · a live hired Workforce, not a mock
ER-4 · every proof composes, adds no layer
the done condition — now three rules
the one committed owner — decides or builds it
consumes it, and must not re-decide it — not a wait
conditional — applies once that row is filed
MET — satisfied, with what satisfied it recorded
NO CHILD — nothing in the set produces this
A blank cell is different: the row does not touch that rule.
Three empty cells on the diagonal are the finding: each exit proof is its own rule in its own column, and every one is unowned. The done condition is owned in zero parts.
Kitchen-sink FIX-1455 no longer has a column — it left the set on Sep 20 (D9). ER-1, ER-2 and ER-3 were re-owned rather than left pointing at it; ER-3 was rewritten.
ER-15 was rewritten (this epic drives no child epic) and ER-19 retired, replaced by the three rules on the bottom row. FIX-1458 has had no column since it was canceled.
Nineteen further rules need no column and bind every row equally: 13 prohibitions (ER-5–14, 22, 24, 25), 4 run-the-set (ER-15–17, 23), 2 further proofs (ER-20, 21).
The set is open (ER-23) — a child filed against any of the three bottom-row cells takes that column and inherits every rule.
